breaking.title: Atiku outlines security and agricultural priorities at Sokoto campaign
breaking.description: Former Nigerian Vice-President Atiku Abubakar addressed supporters in Sokoto during the ADC presidential campaign launch. He pledged to prioritise national security, reopen the country's land borders, facilitate Hajj activities and promote agricultural development.

breaking.description: Trade unions and student organisations are participating in nationwide demonstrations over wages, purchasing power, public services and education. Authorities announced the deployment of 70,000 police officers and gendarmes, with more than 220 public demonstrations expected.

featured.title: Atiku's Sokoto Campaign: A New Test for Nigeria's Opposition
featured.subtitle: Campaign mobilisation, economic promises and the battle for political relevance ahead of 2027
featured.content:
The African Democratic Congress has taken another significant step towards Nigeria's 2027 presidential election with the launch of Atiku Abubakar's presidential campaign activities in Sokoto.

The former Vice-President addressed supporters on Wednesday, 4 November 2026. He was accompanied by his running mate, Rotimi Amaechi, former Sokoto governor Aminu Tambuwal and other prominent opposition figures.

Atiku used the occasion to outline priorities including national security, agricultural development, reopening Nigeria's land borders, facilitating Hajj activities and improving economic opportunities.

His campaign also comes against the backdrop of widespread public concern about the cost of living, unemployment and insecurity.

Rotimi Amaechi called for peaceful political participation and warned against individuals seeking to create tension or disrupt public order.

The campaign has attracted attention because of the broader political competition between the APC and opposition parties ahead of 2027.

However, the opposition's challenge extends beyond organising large rallies. It must demonstrate national organisation, political cooperation and a credible programme capable of addressing Nigeria's economic and security challenges.

For President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the APC, the growing opposition campaign represents another test of public confidence in the administration's policies.

RADIANTWAVES ANALYSIS: Campaign attendance demonstrates political mobilisation, but it does not automatically translate into electoral victory. Nigerians deserve clear policy commitments, credible financing plans, accountability and measurable results from every presidential candidate.

topStories.title: Atiku decries economic hardship during Sokoto campaign
topStories.summary: The ADC campaign has presented the Sokoto turnout as evidence of public dissatisfaction with economic hardship. Meanwhile, Emir Muhammadu Sanusi II has acknowledged improvements in some economic indicators under Tinubu while noting that significant challenges remain.

topStories.title: Atiku arrives in Sokoto amid campaign facility dispute
topStories.summary: Atiku arrived in Sokoto for the ADC campaign launch amid disagreements concerning access to campaign facilities. The party called on Nigerians to consider the implications of the 2026 US midterm elections for political accountability.

topStories.title: Police investigate attack on Peter Obi's convoy in Calabar
topStories.summary: Police arrested a suspect following an attack involving Peter Obi's convoy in Calabar. Political responsibility for the attack should not be assumed without the findings of an investigation.

topStories.title: Democrats take control of both chambers of US Congress
topStories.summary: The Democratic victory creates a new legislative balance in Washington. The incoming Congress will have greater powers to scrutinise the administration and challenge proposed legislation.

topStories.title: France faces major nationwide strike action
topStories.summary: Workers and students are protesting over wages, purchasing power, education and public services. Transport and schools are among the services affected.

topStories.title: South Africa's ANC faces growing electoral pressure
topStories.summary: Early municipal election results indicate a close contest between the ANC and DA. Voter concerns include crime, corruption and the delivery of basic services.

topStories.title: Cyberattack targets French plasma-storage facilities
topStories.summary: A cyberattack attempted to manipulate refrigeration settings at three French plasma-storage facilities. Monitoring systems alerted staff, allowing products to be secured before any were compromised.

articles.title: Nigeria's 2027 election: The opposition's challenge goes beyond campaign crowds
articles.content:
Nigeria's opposition parties are entering another important phase of political competition.

The Sokoto campaign has demonstrated the ADC's willingness to challenge the ruling APC, but the larger question is whether opposition leaders can establish a coordinated national strategy.

Security, economic recovery, employment, infrastructure and institutional accountability should form the foundation of the political debate.

The opposition must explain how it intends to finance its proposals and how it will measure performance if elected.

The APC, meanwhile, must defend its record and explain how its economic and security policies will improve the lives of ordinary Nigerians.

Ultimately, voters should judge political parties by their programmes, performance and commitment to democratic institutions.

articles.title: America's midterm elections reshape Washington
articles.content:
The 2026 US midterm elections have produced a major political setback for President Donald Trump.

Democrats have secured control of both the House of Representatives and Senate.

The new congressional majority will have greater powers to scrutinise government decisions, investigate the administration and influence legislation.

However, President Trump remains in office and retains his constitutional executive powers.

The result demonstrates the importance of midterm elections as a mechanism through which voters can influence the balance of political power.

articles.title: France's nationwide strikes expose continuing social tensions
articles.content:
France is experiencing a major day of nationwide demonstrations involving trade unions, students and workers.

The protests concern wages, purchasing power, education funding, employment and public services.

The French Interior Ministry announced that 70,000 police officers and gendarmes would be deployed, with more than 220 public demonstrations expected.

Transport disruptions and school closures are among the immediate effects.

The demonstrations place additional pressure on the government of President Emmanuel Macron as France continues to debate economic policy and the future of public services.

articles.title: South Africa's municipal elections test the ANC's political strength
articles.content:
South Africa's municipal elections are being closely watched as an indicator of public confidence in the country's established political parties.

Preliminary results reported by Reuters show the ANC leading the DA, although the gap is narrow.

The early count suggests that the ANC is facing continued pressure from voters concerned about crime, corruption and failures in basic services.

However, the results remain incomplete and should not be treated as final national figures.

The elections could also influence coalition arrangements in municipalities where no party secures an outright majority.

articles.title: Cybersecurity becomes essential to protecting medical infrastructure
articles.content:
The reported cyberattack involving French plasma-storage facilities highlights the vulnerability of connected infrastructure.

Cybersecurity is no longer limited to protecting websites, computers and financial information.

Medical facilities, industrial systems, refrigeration equipment and essential public services increasingly depend on connected technologies.

Organisations must invest in monitoring, secure access controls, incident response and staff training.

The protection of digital infrastructure is now directly connected to public safety and national resilience.

radiantWavesPerspective.title: Journalism That Matters
radiantWavesPerspective.content:
The events unfolding across Nigeria and the wider world demonstrate that democracy requires more than political competition.

Citizens need reliable information, responsible leadership and institutions that protect their interests.

From Sokoto to Washington, Paris and Johannesburg, the central question remains the same: how effectively are leaders responding to the needs of the people?

RadiantWaves Media believes journalism must go beyond headlines. It must provide context, examine competing claims, ask difficult questions and help audiences understand the decisions shaping their future.
